cards.note: The waystone which says "AH48" can be found on the road from the Indian border all the way up to Thimphu.
The Bhutan white pine (pinus bhutanica) acan be found most commonly in the red spots.
The Blue (Himalayan) pine is generally only found in the center or west of the country.
That's the buddha statue you can sometimes see in Thimphu.
The Bumthang Airport in Jakar is located in a wet valley.
On the road going up to Trashigang, you can see a grey/black object poking out of the right side of the car.
In this section, you can see a black stick poking out the left part of the car.
Inbetween Wangdue Phodrang and Trongsa, you can find white diagonal lines on the back of the car.
In and around the town of Ha, you can see a hook on the car. It will be very blurred, with only the top being visible.
Between the town of Samkhang and (roughly) the border between Sarpang and Zhemgang district, you can see a very small circle on the right side of the car.
On this part of the road, you can find two white dots on the back of the car; a bigger one, and a smaller one.
In pink, the parts where you'll find a white stripe on the left side of the car.

On this road heading up towards Lhuntse, you can find waystones saying either "DR46" or "DR47".

If you find yourself in a noticeably flat location, you might just be in the south. In fact, that'll almost certainly be where you are.

Coverage here is limited to the towns of Phuntsholing, Sarpang, Gelephu and Samdrup Jongkhar.
The most notable place you can find fog is around Gedu.
If you see lots of fog, or find yourself in a place you'd run into lots of the aforementioned fog, and you're not on the road to Thimphu, you're likely not too far south of Galechugaon.
Gelephu airport is the only airport located in the flat south of the county, making it recognizable.
If you find yourself on flat terrain, on a pebbled road such as this, you're in Gelephu. (Not city center though)

"Late sunset coverage can be found in two places in the country; on a small rural sideroad in the east of Mongar District and in a significantly more urban area around the town of Paro in the west."

The NH2 is this whole northern thing. It seems like.
On this road you'll find the waystone saying "NH4".
You'll sometimes see palms in the southern parts of the country. (Not just the towns in the south)
This airport will be found in a dry northwest valley.
If you see concrete pavement reminiscent of the Philippines, you're in this extension of Phuentsholing.
The Phobjika valley is a wide, relatively flat agricultural valley. It's the largest open valley without a river on Street View.
In the north, you're going to see pines. You can see a lot of them, all over the mountains.

One of, if not the best meta for Bhutan, is that you will always see solid white lines on the outside, on the road going up to Thimphu. Moreover, the quality of the road in comparison to other roads is also noticeable.

This section of the road can feel like road work is in progress, or have a road work vibe, with lots of rocks lying next to the road, and a bunch of sand. Additionaly, you can almost always see a river to the same side of the road in this section.
Sikkim Fir (Abies Densa) can be found in quite a few places, but a high concentration of them should lean you towards Phrumsengla national park. More specifically, northwest of Sengor.
When encountering an SL1 Waystone, it should put you on the SL1.
In the red circle, the area where SL2 waystones should be found.
The SL4 Waystone can be found on this road. You have more chance of seeing a waystone with the SL4 on it in the red part.
SNH Waystones are found on the road from Trashigang to Trashiyangtse in the north.

This kerb, with grey sections seperated by a bit of white, is characteristic for the road leading up to Thimphu. Also, (roughly) between Chimaka and Chapcha, the average length of the grey section tends to be a little smaller, making it look a bit more like a square.
